title: Momentum & Collisions
summary: Momentum $p=mv$ changes by impulse $J=F\Delta t=\Delta p$. In an isolated system total momentum is conserved. Collisions are elastic (KE conserved) or inelastic (KE lost); perfectly inelastic collisions stick together.

conservation of momentum.plain: Total momentum constant with no external force.

concept_sections.heading: Momentum and impulse
concept_sections.explanation: Momentum is $p=mv$; a force acting over time delivers impulse $J=F\Delta t=\Delta p$. Longer contact time means smaller force for the same change.

concept_sections.heading: Conservation of momentum
concept_sections.explanation: With no external force, total momentum is unchanged. Set total momentum before equal to after.

concept_sections.heading: Elastic vs inelastic
concept_sections.explanation: Elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy; inelastic ones don't. Perfectly inelastic collisions stick together and lose the most KE.

concept_sections.heading: Perfectly inelastic collisions
concept_sections.explanation: When objects stick, momentum conservation gives one common final velocity: $m_1v_1+m_2v_2=(m_1+m_2)v_f$.

concept_sections.heading: Impulse and safety
concept_sections.explanation: Extending a collision's duration lowers the peak force ($F=\Delta p/\Delta t$) — why we use airbags, padding, and follow-through.

real_world_examples.title: Catching an egg gently
real_world_examples.scenario: You move your hands back to catch it.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Lengthening the stopping time reduces the force, so the egg survives.

real_world_examples.title: Rocket launch
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Momentum conservation propels the rocket up with equal-and-opposite momentum.

real_world_examples.title: A car crash
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: An inelastic collision conserves momentum while losing kinetic energy to deformation.

problems.prompt: Find the momentum of a $4$ kg cart at $5$ m/s.
A $15$ N force acts for $3$ s. Find the impulse.
A $3$ kg ball at $4$ m/s sticks to a $1$ kg ball at rest. Find their speed.
A $0.4$ kg ball hits a wall at $5$ m/s and bounces at $5$ m/s. Find the impulse.
A $50$ kg skater throws a $4$ kg ball at $6$ m/s. Find her recoil speed.
A $2000$ kg truck at $15$ m/s hits a stopped $1000$ kg car; they stick. Find their speed.
Equal masses collide elastically, one at $8$ m/s, one at rest. Find the final speeds.
solution_steps: First stops, second moves at $8$ m/s.
